name: Zopiclone
lead: Zopiclone is a prescription nonbenzodiazepine hypnotic of the cyclopyrrolone class used for short-term treatment of severe insomnia in adults. It acts at the benzodiazepine site of the GABA-A receptor.[1]

Grokipedia reports it was first patented in 1972 and marketed from 1986 by Rhone-Poulenc under names such as Imovane and Zimovane; it is not approved in the United States, where its (S)-enantiomer eszopiclone is used.[1]
It has no appearance indication. On looksmax.org it appears in occasional threads about sleep aids.[2]
infobox: Prescription-only; not approved in the US[1]

paras: Zopiclone is indicated for short-term treatment of severe insomnia causing distress or functional impairment, with treatment typically limited to about four weeks.[1]

Common effects include a bitter taste, drowsiness, dizziness and dry mouth; more serious risks include anterograde amnesia, behavioural changes such as hallucinations or agitation, tolerance, dependence and rebound insomnia on stopping.[1] A review of case reports and epidemiological data examined abuse and dependence potential for zolpidem and zopiclone.[6]

A randomised trial compared cognitive behavioural therapy with zopiclone for chronic insomnia in older adults.[4] A BMJ meta-analysis examined short-term sedative hypnotics including zopiclone in older people.[3] An observational study examined road-traffic accidents and benzodiazepine use.[5] A Lancet network meta-analysis covers hypnotics for insomnia.[7] A registered trial compared eszopiclone with zopiclone.[8] No studies of appearance outcomes were found.

timeline.event: Rhone-Poulenc introduces zopiclone to the market.[1]

lore.intro: Zopiclone is mentioned in occasional looksmax.org threads on sleep aids and long-term use.[2]

claims.claim: Sleeping pills like zopiclone improve sleep but harm sleep quality over time.
claims.believers: One looksmax.org user wrote that sleep drugs of all kinds interfere with REM sleep and sleep cycles, so people fall asleep but get poor-quality sleep; another said dependence is the side effect.[2]
claims.experts: Reviews describe tolerance, dependence and rebound insomnia as risks of hypnotics, and trial evidence compared CBT with zopiclone in older adults.[1][4]

card.summary: A prescription Z-drug sleeping pill (Imovane); not US-approved and untested for looks.
card.note: Dependence and tolerance risks; not approved in the US.

quick.overview:
Zopiclone is a prescription sleeping pill used in Europe, Canada and elsewhere for short-term severe insomnia.

It has not been tested for appearance; forum mentions are about sleep.
quick.mechanism: It enhances GABA-A receptor signalling at the benzodiazepine site, causing sedation.
quick.risks: Reported effects include drowsiness, bitter taste, amnesia, behavioural changes, tolerance and dependence; treatment is usually limited to about four weeks.
